cards.headline: White lives: it captures Black's atari stone, and Black cannot recapture. The solver's narrow area counts A14 as Black's wall, which turns that capture into a ko.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line: Black 1 is a wrong first move, and White 2 takes the vital point. After White 4 the tree marks the leaf S[ALIVE]; the solver said KO.

Black 5 ataris the White stone above it, but White 6 captures Black 5 and still has a liberty at A14, so Black cannot recapture. Black 7 takes that liberty, and White 8 connects. After White 10, C19 is an eye, and capturing Black's corner stones gives the second.

text: The tree is right. Every Black move at the leaf other than Black 5 leaves White alive, as the solver proves, and Black 5 fails as Diagram 2 shows.

The solver said KO because its narrow search area counts A14 as Black's wall, as if Black 7 were already there: then White 6 has one liberty, and the capture becomes a ko. The wider area, with A14 open, did not overturn this: with unlimited Black ko threats its search stays undecided after Black 5, though it proves White alive after White 6 at once. At the leaf, that search is at the edge of its budget.
